# 1. Project Definition
## 1.1. Project Theme

The selected project theme is Urban Rental Housing Price Analytics, with Mumbai selected as the geographical focus of the analysis.

The project aims to develop a rental price prediction model using property characteristics , geographical location, and neighbourhood amenities.

The analysis will subsequently compare observed rental prices with model-predicted prices to identify potentially over-priced and under-priced properties and neighbourhoods.

The findings will be considered from both tenant and investor perspectives.

## 1.2. Selected Analysis Type
## Predictive Analytics

Predictive analytics has been selected as the first type of analytics to investigate.

This choice is motivated by the primary objective of estimating the expected monthly rental price of a residential property based on its characteristics, location, and surrounding neighbourhood.


The predicted rental price can be subsequently compared with the observed market rent to support the identification of potentially over-priced and under-priced properties.

## 1.3. Research Question

Can monthly rental prices of residential properties in Mumbai be predicted using property characteristics, geographic location, and accessibility to neighbourhood amenities?

## 1.4. Required Datasets

To answer the research question, the project will require data describing individual rental properties as well as information about their surrounding neighbourhoods.

The rental property dataset should ideally contain:
Monthly rental price
Property type
Number of bedrooms
Number of bathrooms
Property area
Furnishing status
Floor information (eg. sqft area, super buildup area)
Parking availability
Locality or neighbourhood
Geographic coordinates, if available

The monthly rental price will be used as the target variable in the predictive model.

Additional amenities and geographic accessibility will also be investigated, such as:
Bus stops
Metro Stations
Railway Stations
Airport
Schools
Hospitals
Parks

## 1.5. Data Access Plan

The rental property data will initially be investigated through publicly available datasets and open-data repositories.

Potential sources include publicly available real-estate datasets, Kaggle, and relevant government or city open-data portals.

Neighbourhood and amenity information will be investigated through geographic and open-data sources such as OpenStreetMap and relevant Mumbai or Maharashtra open-data portals.

The datasets will be evaluated based on:
Availability of rental price information
Availability of relevant property characteristics
Availability of geographic location
Number of Observations
Data completeness
Geographic coverage of Mumbai
Compatibility between datasets
Accessibility and licensing conditions

The final dataset selection will be made after comparing the available data resources.

## 1.6 Dataset Investigation

### 1.6.1 Objective

The objective was to identify suitable datasets for predicting monthly residential rents in Mumbai and determine whether they support the research question:

"Can monthly rental prices in Mumbai be predicted using property characteristics and geographic location, with neighbourhood amenities as a planned extension?"

### 1.6.2 Search Strategy and Evaluation

Five CSV files obtained from Kaggle were inspected for price type, property characteristics, Mumbai coverage, location information, record count, data quality and licensing.

| Dataset | Records | Price type | Coverage | Decision |
| `Mumbai_property_details.csv` | 23,398 | Monthly rent | Mumbai | Selected as main dataset |
| `data.csv` | 7,691 total; 1,719 Mumbai | Monthly rent | Five cities | Retained for possible external validation |
| `mumbai_flats.csv` | 9,955 | Sale price | Mumbai | Excluded |
| `data_for_model.csv` | 7,483 | Sale price | Mumbai | Excluded |
| `data_v_1.csv` | 2,601 | Sale price | Mumbai | Excluded |

The three sale-price datasets were excluded because sale prices and monthly rents measure different things and cannot be used interchangeably.

### 1.6.3 Selected Dataset

Main dataset: `Mumbai_property_details.csv`

This dataset was selected because it contains the largest identified collection of Mumbai rental listings and a useful range of property characteristics.

The main variables for analysis are:

- Target: Monthly rent (`Price`), to be converted into numeric rupees.
- Property characteristics: BHK, bathrooms, area, furnishing, balconies, floor, year of construction and property type.
- Location: To be extracted and standardized from listing titles or descriptions.
- Additional variable: Building amenities, where sufficiently complete.

### 1.6.4 Key Limitations and Planned Cleaning

The selected dataset has several limitations that must be addressed before modelling:

- Price and area formats: Rent values contain text such as “1.4 Lac”, while the area field appears to contain scraping artefacts.
- Location: There is no dedicated locality column or geographic coordinates, so locality extraction and standardization will be required.
- Duplicates and outliers: Repeated listings and implausible values must be identified and reviewed.
- Missing data: Some variables have substantial missingness; columns with too many missing values may be excluded.


### 1.6.5 Investigation Outcome and Next Steps

`Mumbai_property_details.csv` is the provisional main dataset because of its size and range of rental-property variables. `data.csv` is a potential external validation source, while the three sale-price datasets have been excluded.

### 1.6.6 Source Details

Main dataset URL: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/harshalhonde/property-rental-listings-dataset
Dataset collaborator: Harshal H (Owner)

The objective of this stage is to import the rental dataset into RStudio and examine its structure, variables, and suitability for predicting monthly rental prices in Mumbai.


rent_data <- read.csv("data/Mumbai_property_details.csv")
head(rent_data)
names(rent_data)
dim(rent_data)
str(rent_data)


## 1.7.1 Data Quality Assessment

# Count missing or blank values in each column
missing_values <- sapply(rent_data, function(x) {
  sum(is.na(x) | trimws(as.character(x)) == "")
})

missing_values

# Calculate the percentage of missing values
missing_percentage <- round(
  missing_values / nrow(rent_data) * 100, 2
)

missing_summary <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(rent_data),
  Missing_Count = missing_values,
  Missing_Percentage = missing_percentage
)

missing_summary

# Check for completely duplicated rows
sum(duplicated(rent_data))

# Check the number of unique values in each column
sapply(rent_data, function(x) length(unique(x)))

# Inspect some price and area values
head(rent_data[, c("Price", "Area", "BHK", "Location")], 10)


### Initial Data Quality Findings

The dataset contains 23,405 records and 18 variables. The initial
assessment identified missing values in several variables and
3,111 completely duplicated rows.

The Price and Area columns contain no more than two and zero
missing values, respectively, according to the initial check.
However, both columns require further inspection because Price
contains text-based values such as "1.4 Lac", while Area contains
values such as "750 12800".

Ownership has the highest proportion of missing values (87.89%),
followed by Balconies (55.62%) and Year.of.Construction (36.40%).
These variables will require careful consideration before model
development.

The Location column contains only one unique value, Mumbai.
Neighbourhood-level information will therefore need to be
investigated separately.

## 1.7.4 Preparing Variables for Analysis

# Create a working copy; preserve the original dataset
rent_clean <- rent_data

# Extract the first number from Area
area_parts <- strsplit(
  trimws(rent_clean$Area),
  "\\s+"
)

area_first <- sapply(area_parts, `[`, 1)

# Convert the extracted area to numeric
rent_clean$Area_original <- rent_clean$Area
rent_clean$Area_sqft <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(area_first)
)

# Convert rent prices to numeric rupees
price_text <- tolower(trimws(rent_clean$Price))
price_text <- gsub(",", "", price_text)

rent_clean$Monthly_Rent <- sapply(price_text, function(p) {
  if (is.na(p) || p == "") {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  if (grepl("lac", p)) {
    return(as.numeric(sub("[^0-9.].*$", "", p)) * 100000)
  }

  if (grepl("crore|cr", p)) {
    return(as.numeric(sub("[^0-9.].*$", "", p)) * 10000000)
  }

  suppressWarnings(
    as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", p))
  )
})

# Inspect the new variables
head(
  rent_clean[, c(
    "Price", "Monthly_Rent",
    "Area_original", "Area_sqft"
  )],
  15
)

# Check conversion failures
sum(!is.na(rent_clean$Price) &
      trimws(rent_clean$Price) != "" &
      is.na(rent_clean$Monthly_Rent))

sum(!is.na(rent_clean$Area_sqft))
summary(rent_clean$Monthly_Rent)
summary(rent_clean$Area_sqft)
